scientific_question: Do CA1 reactive astrocyte hotspots occupy locally pyramidal-depleted niches, relative to baseline astrocyte hotspots, and does that focal neuron-loss pattern add signal beyond the current CA1 gliosis panel?
approach: Assign cells to CA1 from CustomAnnotations polygons. From ClassificationNode labels, collect CA1 Reactive Astrocyte, Astrocyte, and Pyramidal Neuron centroids. Define CA1 reactive hotspot cells as reactive astrocytes with at least 3 same-class neighbors within 70 px; define baseline astrocyte hotspot cells analogously among Astrocytes. For each hotspot cell, count CA1 pyramidal neighbors within a contact radius and summarize the mean log1p neighbor count. The donor biomarker is mean_log1p_pyramidal_neighbors_around_astrocyte_hotspots minus mean_log1p_pyramidal_neighbors_around_reactive_hotspots, so larger values indicate reactive hotspots sit in more pyramidal-depleted niches than ordinary astrocyte hotspots.

variations.name: candidate_variant_a
variations.description: Hotspots defined with same-class radius 70 px and k>=3; pyramidal neighbor counts measured within 70 px of each hotspot cell.

variations.name: candidate_variant_b
variations.description: Same hotspot definition, but use a stricter 50 px pyramidal-neighbor radius to focus on immediate pericellular depletion.

notes: Use centroid-based radius queries only; contour areas are not needed here. Annotation polygons are stored at 16x cell coordinates, so divide polygon coordinates by 16 before CA1 assignment. Handle low-count cases gracefully and avoid donor-specific fallbacks.
rationale: Rounds 5 and 6 suggest that CA1 reactive hotspot architecture is real, but the neuron-facing hotspot exposure feature added only modestly after the larger microclustering gain, implying that simple exposure may already be partly saturated by the existing pyramidal-burden and niche terms. The right next test is to keep the same successful CA1 reactive-hotspot lead while changing one operator: instead of asking how many pyramidal neurons see hotspots, ask whether reactive hotspots themselves sit in neuron-sparse CA1 territory. That is biologically interpretable as focal gliotic scarring or local neuronal dropout, and it could either add new signal or replace the weaker earlier neuron-adjacent niche member with a cleaner hotspot-centered version.
